issues.description: Directory entries with traversal names are handled in Unzip.initExtractFile via mkdirs and never reach UnzipEngine.unzipFile, so our sink-level check does not cover them; a malicious directory entry could still create directories outside the destination. The official fix guards this in initExtractFile before the isDirectory() branch.
The diff commits unrelated Maven build artifacts (target/maven-archiver/pom.properties, createdFiles.lst, inputFiles.lst), reducing minimality and cleanliness of the patch.

result.root_cause: Archive entry names containing path-traversal sequences flow untrusted into a File written to disk without verifying the resolved path stays inside the extraction destination directory (zip slip).
result.summary: Our patch adds a canonical-path containment check (assertFileWithinDestination) at the actual file-write sink in UnzipEngine.unzipFile, which is the CWE-022 defense-of-record and even hardens the separator-boundary edge case the official fix misses. The POV no longer reproduces and the regression passed. It differs from the official fix in location (UnzipEngine vs Unzip.initExtractFile) and, importantly, does not guard traversal in directory-only entries which are created via mkdirs in initExtractFile without invoking unzipFile — a real but lower-impact completeness gap. Overall a sound, class-level fix for file writes with one uncovered sibling path and some committed build-artifact noise.
